en: The Banaue Rice Terraces use the inclined plane principle to help farmers carry crops up steep mountain slopes with less effort.
The rough bark of a Narra tree creates high friction, allowing monkeys to grip the trunk tightly while climbing.
Falling coconuts from tall coconut trees accelerate toward the ground because Earth's gravity pulls them straight down.
Volcanic black sand beaches in Camiguin contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic mineral that can pick up small iron filings.
During dry summer months, touching a metal jeepney door handle can cause a small static electric shock.
A rainbow appears over Taal Lake after a rainstorm because water droplets refract and reflect sunlight into different colors.
Shouting inside the limestone caves of Sagada produces a clear echo because sound waves bounce off the hard rock walls.
Dark basalt rocks on a sunny beach in Camiguin absorb more heat from the sun than light-colored coral sand.
The rushing water of Maria Cristina Falls possesses high kinetic energy, which is converted into electrical energy at the hydroelectric plant.
The human jaw acts as a third-class lever when biting into a hard green mango, with the jaw muscles providing the effort.
Striking a hollowed bamboo slit drum converts mechanical energy from the mallet into sound energy that echoes across the village.
A rolling boulder at the top of a steep Cordillera mountain has high gravitational potential energy before it starts falling.
